You can do it in paint. Changing a single pixel won't do much.

Q mentioned 32 points of comparison - but not how large of an area they are using. If it's a simple pixel comparison (seems dumb, but what do I know), then you just have to get enough of the right pixels to not match. In that case, skewing the image might work, or add a little rotation (~5*)and a slight resize (83%). Rotation adds a lot of processing time, as does scaling.

Adding some bars might help foil a scanner - especially if they are slightly irregular. Like a picture of someone in jail, but the bars have been bent in various ways.

OCR tools are good at reading all sorts of characters, so anything that breaks the edges that form a character may help. Some OCR tools can't handle a line through a word, but a pattern matching tool would still see the word. So then you need to make it hard for SW to pick out the edge locations. Making a word skewed (like the Star Wars opening text) with some random rotation to the characters is going to force someone to crank up the OCR parameters and seriously increase the processing time required on each image.

Misspelled words (or missing characters) can help make it harder for automated tools to pick out specific words.
